algorithm.adjust_even_tail: when the length is even and the hole equals (length - 2) // 2, the lone left child at 2 * hole + 1 moves up into the hole and the hole becomes that child; this is the only case in which a hole at or above the last-parent bound still has a child in range
algorithm.adjust_push_up: while the hole is below its start index and its parent is strictly below the value (unsigned lexicographic order), the parent moves down and the hole becomes the parent; then the value is stored in the hole
algorithm.adjust_sift_down: while the hole is below the last-parent bound (length - 1) // 2, the larger of the two children (indices 2 * hole + 1 and 2 * hole + 2) moves up into the hole; the right child wins exact ties, because the second child's comparison falls through to it on equality
algorithm.adjust_value_precondition: the value is at most every ancestor above the original hole, as in both binary uses (heapify passes the hole's own element; the pop loop passes a leaf element with the hole at the root, so the push-up never needs to rise above the original hole)
algorithm.depth: signed budget in rdx; tested for exact zero, decremented once per partition level at 0x5d4a429; the recursive call and the tail iteration both use the decremented depth
algorithm.entry_small_range: byte count at most 0x100 (16 elements) returns immediately at 0x5d4a697, sorting nothing; the caller runs the final insertion sort over such ranges
algorithm.heapsort_heapify: adjust_heap is called for hole indices (count - 2) // 2 down to 0, each with the element at that hole as the value, at 0x5d4a62d
algorithm.heapsort_pop: the last element is swapped with the first and adjust_heap is called with hole 0, the remaining count and the old last element as the value, at 0x5d4a66f; the loop body also runs once with the last element at begin + 1, which swaps the final two elements into ascending order
algorithm.heapsort_trigger: depth exactly zero at entry jumps to 0x5d4a5fd (whole range), and a decremented depth of zero after a partition jumps to 0x5d4a600 (left part); either way the routine returns after the heapsort, with no further recursion
algorithm.median_candidates: second element (begin + 0x10), middle element (begin + (byte count >> 5 << 4), i.e. element index count // 2) and last element (end - 0x10); the median of the three is moved to begin
algorithm.median_network: compare second against middle: below takes the 0x5d4a458 arm, at or above takes the 0x5d4a520 arm; each arm compares against last and swaps begin with middle (0x5d4a478), begin with last (0x5d4a54d) or begin with second (0x5d4a590); equal first qwords fall through to a second-qword comparison, and exact equality follows the greater-or-equal arm
algorithm.median_shared_seconds_block: the 0x5d4a53f seconds block is shared by the 0x5d4a683 equal-first arm and the 0x5d4a520 fallthrough; a middle first qword above last's is unreachable in the fallthrough because it would contradict the second element being at or above middle while sharing last's first qword
algorithm.order: ascending unsigned lexicographic order on (first qword, second qword); all comparisons are unsigned (jb/jae on the first qword, then on the second qword when the first qwords are equal)
algorithm.partition_cursors: left cursor starts at begin + 0x10, right cursor at end; the left scan advances while the element is strictly below the pivot, the right scan retreats (reading end - 0x10 downward) while the element is strictly above it, and a swap exchanges the stopped pair and advances the left cursor
algorithm.partition_cut: when the left cursor reaches or passes the right cursor element, the cut is the left cursor; the recursive call sorts [cut, end) and the tail iteration continues on [begin, cut); on return, every element in [begin, cut) is at most the pivot and every element in [cut, end) is at least it
algorithm.partition_guard: the scans are unguarded; they cannot run out of range after the median step because at least one candidate at or above the pivot and at least one at or below it remain inside the range
algorithm.pivot: the element at begin after the median step; it stays at begin through the partition
algorithm.recursion_tail: after the recursive call, a left byte count at most 0x100 returns, a decremented depth of zero heapsorts the left part, otherwise the tail iteration reuses the same depth on [begin, cut)
